titulo.alumno: «È possibile che arrivi»: opinion, certainty and the future

intro: The present subjunctive coexists with the indicative and the future: the mood you choose shows how sure you are of what you say. Mastering this contrast gives you precision as a B1 speaker.

texto: **So che arriva** (I know he arrives; certainty: indicative). **Penso che arrivi** (I think he arrives; opinion: subjunctive). **È possibile che arrivi** (it's possible that he arrives; hypothesis: subjunctive).
Certainty takes the indicative; probability or doubt takes the subjunctive.

With expressions of doubt about the future you can use the present subjunctive or the future: **Spero che arrivi domani** = **Spero che arriverà domani**. Both are correct; the subjunctive sounds more refined.

filas.texto: So che Marco è a casa.
Penso che Marco sia a casa.
È possibile che Marco arrivi tardi.

frases.estudio: Sai se Marco e Giulia vengono stasera?
frases.alumno: Do you know whether Marco and Giulia are coming this evening?
analisis: Marco and Giulia are coming this evening

frases.estudio: So che Marco è già partito dall'ufficio, ma è possibile che arrivi tardi per il traffico.
frases.alumno: I know that Marco has already left the office, but it's possible that he arrives late because of the traffic.
analisis: so che Marco è già partito
I know that Marco has already left
ma è possibile che arrivi tardi
but it's possible that he arrives late

frases.estudio: Penso che sia ancora a casa. Mi ha detto che aveva mal di testa.
frases.alumno: I think she is still at home. She told me she had a headache.
analisis: penso che sia ancora a casa
I think she is still at home

pregunta.texto: Why does Matteo say «so che Marco è partito» with the indicative?

opciones.texto: Because it expresses a verified certainty of which he is fully informed.
opciones.explicacion: «Sapere» in a positive assertion conveys certainty and takes the indicative.

opciones.texto: Because he doubts whether Marco works in that office.
opciones.explicacion: There is no doubt at all about Marco's departure.

opciones.texto: Because it is an indirect question.
opciones.explicacion: It is a categorical affirmative statement.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the loro (they) form of «arrivare» in the present subjunctive.

frase.texto: È probabile che i nostri amici ___ prima di cena.

opciones.texto: arrivino
opciones.explicacion: Third person plural ending of the present subjunctive (-are → -ino).

opciones.texto: arrivano
opciones.explicacion: It is the present indicative: «they arrive».

opciones.texto: arriveranno
opciones.explicacion: It is the simple future of the indicative.

pregunta.texto: What degree of certainty does this sentence reflect?

frase.texto: Penso che sia ancora a casa.

opciones.texto: An opinion or conjecture not confirmed one hundred per cent.
opciones.explicacion: «Pensare che» qualifies the statement with the present subjunctive.

opciones.texto: An absolute certainty backed by official documents.
opciones.explicacion: It lacks direct visual confirmation.

opciones.texto: A firm order for him to stay at home.
opciones.explicacion: It is an estimate of his current whereabouts.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the lui (he) form of «arrivare» in the present subjunctive.

frase.texto: È possibile che Marco ___ in ritardo a causa del traffico.

opciones.texto: arrivi
opciones.explicacion: Third person of the present subjunctive of «arrivare» after «è possibile che».

opciones.texto: arriva
opciones.explicacion: It is the present indicative, unsuitable for a hypothetical possibility.

opciones.texto: arrivò
opciones.explicacion: It is the indicative past historic.

frase.texto: È possibile che arrivino in ritardo per il traffico intenso

piezas.traduccion: It is possible that they arrive late because of the heavy traffic.
piezas.explicacion: Impersonal hypothesis with the present subjunctive.

pregunta.texto: What is the difference between «so che viene» and «spero che venga»?

opciones.texto: «So che viene» expresses objective certainty; «spero che venga» expresses a personal longing.
opciones.explicacion: The indicative states certainties; the subjunctive channels wishes and doubts.

opciones.texto: Both sentences mean exactly the same, with no nuance at all.
opciones.explicacion: The verb mood changes the speaker's attitude radically.

opciones.texto: «So che viene» refers to the past; «spero che venga» to the present.
opciones.explicacion: Both sentences are anchored in the current perspective.

frase.texto: Non sono sicuro che quel ristorante sia ancora aperto a ___

opciones.texto: quest'ora
opciones.explicacion: Time expression with an apostrophe («quest'ora»).

opciones.texto: quel giorno
opciones.explicacion: It does not match the time sense of the present night.

opciones.texto: mezzogiorno
opciones.explicacion: It would be midday and does not fit the present doubt.

pregunta.texto: Why can the indicative be used after «forse» here?

opciones.texto: Because the adverb «forse» in Italian very commonly allows the indicative mood.
opciones.explicacion: «Forse» does not require the conjunction «che» and is usually combined with the present or future.

opciones.texto: Because «forse» is an absolute synonym of «sicuramente» (certainly).
opciones.explicacion: It means «perhaps», but syntactically it does not require a clause with «che».

opciones.texto: Because the verb «arrivare» lacks subjunctive forms.
opciones.explicacion: «Arrivare» has its complete regular paradigm.
